### Trace persistence limits and sampling rule (2026-11-25)

This completes `sfk-e8baa3796f5c29cdb66f46eb` for the "bounded per-run log quotas" and "log sampling levels" of F2-197. For standard disk-bound logs and traces, the write path runs (1) sensitivity classification, (2) `RedactionSettlement` (F2-195), (3) severity and sampling filter, (4) quota check, and (5) write. When a step drops an event, the later steps skip it. Disk bytes are counted after redaction, as the serialized record written.

**F2-196 local raw debug capture.** After sensitivity classification, FileSafe may write raw payloads covered by F2-196 to a separate local capture only with explicit user opt-in and an unexpired capture. FileSafe encrypts the payload before writing it and applies the capture's expiry to local retention. This write path is outside `TracePersistencePolicy` and `ObservabilityEnvelope`. Raw capture bytes stay out of standard logs and traces, diagnostic and support bundles, and OTLP export. Any request to export the capture itself must warn the user that it contains unredacted data before export.

**`RedactionSettlement` and `ObservabilityEnvelope` fields.** Both records are closed. These tables type the 2026-07-08 field lists above; `ObservabilityEnvelope` also carries `run_id`, `quota_owner_kind` and `quota_owner_id`, which per-run quota accounting needs. `identity_id` and `non_secret_ref` use the like-named definitions in `Plans/source_control_contracts.schema.json`. All timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC strings. All fields are required unless their presence rule says otherwise.

| `RedactionSettlement` field | Type and presence rule |
| --- | --- |
| `settlement_id` | `identity_id`; identifies this exact pre-write decision |
| `source_ref` | `non_secret_ref`; opaque identity of the classified source, never a raw payload or local path |
| `redaction_profile_id` | `identity_id`; exact redaction profile applied |
| `decision` | Closed enum `clean` (content can be written as classified), `redacted` (write the redacted artifact), `blocked` (write no content; count one dropped event) |
| `redacted_artifact_ref` | `non_secret_ref`; present only for `redacted`, names only the sanitized output to be written |
| `blocked_reason_code` | Non-empty string; present only for `blocked`, carrying the redaction owner's reason code and no raw text |
| `created_at_utc` | UTC timestamp of settlement |

| `ObservabilityEnvelope` field | Type and presence rule |
| --- | --- |
| `envelope_id`, `trace_id` | `identity_id`; exact envelope and trace |
| `run_id` | Required `identity_id` or `null`. The value is the owning run id for run-owned events and `null` for terminal diagnostic logs or user-requested terminal diagnostic bundles that belong to no run (`Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md` SMPFS-076) |
| `quota_owner_kind` | Closed enum `run`, `terminal_session`, `diagnostic_bundle`. A non-null `run_id` requires `run`. A null `run_id` requires `terminal_session` for a session's diagnostic logs or `diagnostic_bundle` for a user-requested terminal diagnostic bundle |
| `quota_owner_id` | `identity_id`; equals `run_id` for `run`, `terminal_session_id` for `terminal_session`, and the bundle request id for `diagnostic_bundle` |
| `event_refs[]` | Non-empty ordered array of unique `non_secret_ref`; references only events covered by this settlement and admitted by filtering and quotas, never discarded content |
| `sampling_policy_id` | `identity_id`; identifies the `TracePersistencePolicy.policy_id` in force when the envelope was created |
| `quota_class` | Closed enum `provider_trace`, `stream` (WebSocket/SSE), `terminal`, `subagent`, `tool`, `mcp`, `memory`, `support_bundle`; all classes share the same per-run total |
| `redaction_settlement_id` | `identity_id`; resolves to the exact `clean` or `redacted` settlement for every event named by the envelope |
| `created_at_utc` | UTC timestamp of envelope creation |

**Quota owner.** Per-run accounting is kept per quota owner. Wherever the quota class, limits, overflow, quota marker and acceptance rules of this section say "run" or "per-run", they mean the envelope's quota owner: its run, or for a runless envelope its terminal session or diagnostic bundle request. `max_bytes_per_run` caps each quota owner. A `terminal_session` owner's quota and diagnostic summary settle when the session closes, and a `diagnostic_bundle` owner's when the bundle is written. The "run's log view" for a runless owner is that terminal tab's diagnostics (SMPFS-076).

**`TracePersistencePolicy` fields and limits.** DL-2602 confirms the defaults of 8 MiB per trace and 256 MiB per run.

| Field | Type | Allowed values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy_id` | `identity_id` | non-empty | — |
| `sampling_level` | enum | `errors`, `standard`, `debug` | `standard` |
| `sample_rate` | number | 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive | 1.0 |
| `max_bytes_per_trace` | integer bytes | 1 MiB to 64 MiB | 8 MiB |
| `max_bytes_per_run` | integer bytes | 16 MiB to 1 GiB, and at least `max_bytes_per_trace` | 256 MiB |
| `terminal_coalesce_ms` | integer ms | 16 to 1000 | 100 |
| `retention_days` | integer days | at least 1 | the retention class `Plans/storage-plan.md` assigns to the log family; this policy references it and never overrides it |
| `redaction_required` | boolean | always `true` for standard trace persistence | `true` |
| `export_allowed` | boolean | `true` only when the user enables the optional OTLP export adapter | `false` |

**Sampling levels.** Event severities are `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`. `errors` persists `error` and `warn`; `standard` adds `info`; `debug` adds `debug` and `trace`, subject to `sample_rate`. `sample_rate` applies only to `debug` and `trace` events and only at level `debug`. The sampling decision is per trace and applies uniformly to all eligible events: its `debug`/`trace` events persist when the first 8 bytes of `sha256(trace_id)`, read as an unsigned big-endian integer and divided by 2^64, are less than `sample_rate`. `error` and `warn` events, and the join events usage needs (attempt start, attempt end, and each usage record carrying `attempt_id`), are never sampled out at any level.

**Terminal diagnostic severity.** At the trace write boundary, including when writing a terminal diagnostic bundle under SMPFS-076, FileSafe maps `TerminalDiagnosticsEnvelope.severity` from the terminal record wire contract in `Plans/Section15_MVP_Promoted_Features_Spec.md`. `info` maps to `info`, `warning` to `warn`, `error` to `error`, and `critical` to `error`. After redaction, FileSafe uses the mapped trace severity for filtering, sampling and reserve eligibility. The serialized terminal record retains its source `severity` and wire shape.

**Terminal streams.** Terminal output is persisted as chunks, never per character: bytes are coalesced and a chunk is written when `terminal_coalesce_ms` has passed since the chunk opened or it reaches 64 KiB, whichever is first.

**Overflow.** Before each write, check whether its serialized redacted bytes would exceed either cap. After crossing the base limit for the trace or the run, only `error`, `warn` and usage join events can use that scope's reserve of 10% of its limit (rounded down to whole bytes). The write must fit both applicable caps, including any available reserve. The writer counts each quota-rejected event once per run even if both caps refuse it. `dropped_bytes` counts the size of those serialized redacted records. A blocked redaction contributes one `dropped_events` and zero `dropped_bytes` because it yields no safe serialized record. Filtering and sampling exclusions are outside these counts. A new run starts with fresh quotas.

**Quota marker.** The trace writer owns one bounded diagnostic summary per exact quota owner (`quota_owner_kind`, `quota_owner_id`). On the first quota refusal it sets one `quota_exceeded` marker on that summary, with `scope: trace | run`, `limit_bytes` and `trace_id` only when `scope=trace`. If both limits refuse the same write, record the run limit. The writer maintains `dropped_events` and `dropped_bytes` as monotonic, saturating unsigned 64-bit totals and publishes the final totals at run settlement. The marker and totals occupy one mutable redacted projection value, at most 1 KiB per run, accounted separately from the trace-event budget. Storage-plan §2.3.1 registration for that diagnostic value is required before durable publication. The projection is not an `EventRecord`; it never rewrites seglog or persists one event per drop. Live accounting stays with the trace writer, and overflow never pauses, fails or slows the run. The run's log view shows "Log limit reached; N events not saved" while the counts are available and shows the limit without a number if the summary cannot be verified.

**Acceptance.** (1) With defaults, fill 32 traces in one run to 8 MiB each of serialized redacted records, with zero drops. Submit a 64 KiB `warn` record to one of those traces. It writes using both reserves and leaves zero drops and no `quota_exceeded` marker. Submit a 32 KiB `info` record to the same trace that passes the severity filter and is outside the usage join set. Both caps refuse it. The run summary now contains exactly one `quota_exceeded` marker with `scope = run` and shows `dropped_events = 1` and `dropped_bytes = 32768`. Then submit a 1 MiB `error` record to the same trace. It fits the run reserve and exceeds the trace reserve. The same marker remains, the two refused records are absent from disk, and the final totals are `dropped_events = 2` and `dropped_bytes = 1081344`. All three submitted sizes are serialized redacted byte sizes. (2) The same `trace_id` and `sample_rate` give the same keep or drop decision on every run and machine. (3) At level `errors`, no `info`, `debug` or `trace` event is on disk, and every admitted usage record still joins by `attempt_id`. (4) A terminal emitting one character per millisecond for 10 s writes at most 10 s / `terminal_coalesce_ms` + 1 chunks. (5) An event whose settlement is `blocked` is never on disk and appears in the dropped count. (6) A terminal session and a user-requested diagnostic bundle outside any run both write envelopes with `run_id = null`. Session diagnostics use `quota_owner_kind = terminal_session` and the `terminal_session_id` as `quota_owner_id`. Bundle writes use `quota_owner_kind = diagnostic_bundle` and the bundle request id as `quota_owner_id`. The same caps, reserve and single marker apply independently to each owner. (7) A run-owned envelope carries a non-null `run_id`, `quota_owner_kind = run` and `quota_owner_id = run_id`. An envelope with a missing `run_id` or a mismatched quota owner fails validation. (8) At a terminal bundle write at level `errors`, `warning` and `critical` records pass the filter and are eligible to write using reserve when their bytes fit both applicable caps. Their serialized `severity` values remain `warning` and `critical`, respectively.

On 2026-11-24 at about 10:40 PM EST, Jared answered card C-FIX79 ("Take the recommended answers to 11 small plan questions?") with "A take all the recommended answers." The answer was relayed to the stream C lead pm-closure-lead (pm-mail 1125033823-33e4). Each answer below is the card's recommended option, and the registry lines are rows of Plans/.audits/_semantic_closure_registry.jsonl.

1. Lines 1470 and 1477, concern labels: the closed sets are the union of values already in use. visibility_level is user_visible | project | restricted; attention_level is info | warning | needs_action; concern_category is coverage_blocker | projection_trust | risk | weak_integration. The concern record and concern.created operation schemas and their storage value registry copies carry these enums, and the Contracts_V0 minimum concern example uses severity error instead of high. Orchestrator_Page OP-004 stays the semantic owner of the concern family.
2. Line 1785, opening DevTools: cmd.browser.open_devtools is a navigation wrapper. Its request is BrowserDevToolsOpenRequest {browser_session_id, mode?: docked_bottom | docked_right | undocked} and its typed route result is BrowserDevToolsOpenResultV1 {devtools_session_id, boundary_ref, opened_at_utc}, both in Plans/section15_browser_program_contracts.schema.json. The wiring rows name them, BrowserActionRequestV2 no longer lists the command, and the DL-341 handler_unavailable refusal for its unsettled request ends.
3. Line 1546, Tools.md duplicate chapters 10 to 13: the physical numbers stay. Chapters of the second block (the second ## 10. Firecrawl provider integration through ## 15.) are cited by heading name and their numbers are not authoritative; the 2026-07-08 supersession's ## 11. target is withdrawn. Permissions PS-058's pinned Tools.md §10.1 citation names its heading. No heading is renamed.
4. Line 1343, LSP client foundation: Puppet Master builds its own client on the LSPSupport §3.6.1 stack (lsp-types, tokio, tokio-util, serde_json, tracing). async-lsp may be used only as an optional internal wire helper. lsp-client and async_lsp_client are rejected alternatives, not dependencies.
5. Line 1381, persona disable and restore: both are typed operations of cmd.persona.update, set_enabled and restore_shipped_default, under the existing expected_owner_revision compare-and-swap and full PERSONA.md validation, and their success is the existing persona.updated. The Personas addendum's cmd.persona.edit, cmd.persona.disable, cmd.persona.restore and cmd.persona.validate_schema spellings are retired.
6. Line 1382, crew roles: crew.roles is the role record map {display_name, description, required_capabilities[], default_persona_id?, allowed_persona_ids[]} keyed by the closed role_id set planner, implementer, reviewer, tester, designer, security, release, governance. owner_hint matches a role_id exactly, the Persona comes from allowed_persona_ids[] or default_persona_id, and provider and model come only from the Models_System selection order. The provider/model/persona tuple form is retired source lineage.
7. Line 1467, Resubmit: the PRDB-014 targeted revision pass is the new command cmd.prd_builder.revision.resubmit, with a UI_Command_Catalog row, a payload definition under PRDB-024, a prd_planning_runtime_contracts entry and the production wiring row catalog.prd_builder_revision_resubmit. FinalGUISpec 7.19.2 bundle Resubmit, F3-150, F3-322 and PRD Builder bind to it. The canonical PRD Builder, Planning Wizard and Plan Compile command set of DL-333 grows from 28 to 29 ids; DL-333's own text is unchanged.
8. Line 1468, persona mapping editors: FinalGUISpec 19.8 and F3-296 narrow to the planning.interview.builder-* settings, saved through the Settings transaction, plus the existing crew and overseer Persona selections. The Interview-stage, Orchestrator node/package/lane/seam and Multi-Pass mapping editors and every per-mapping platform/model choice are retired. Provider-gap disclosures travel in the resolver's skipped_persona_controls[].
9. Line 1469, Free Models: the top-10 is the model defaults list (Settings transaction on ai.models.default-model and its layers), not a second list. Retry check is cmd.model.refresh with refresh_reason free_models_update_retry, and View details is a no-persist disclosure of the failed update's activation, quarantine and rollback records.
10. Line 1533, FinalGUISpec duplicate ## 15 and #### 7.4.2: F3-389 is amended so both pairs stay as declared aliases and citations use the full heading name. Renumbering is left to a scheduled structural cleanup; no heading is renamed.
11. Line 1605, Decisions page: Puppet Master shows no Decisions GUI. The sentence "GUI visibility is through Settings > Governance > Decisions when surfaced by FinalGUISpec" in the 2026-07-08 FABLE Deferred Action Concrete Repair Addendum of this log is retired by this entry, and DecisionRecord gui_surface_ref is always absent. DecisionRecord is the planning-canon shape of a Decision_Log entry. The old entry's text is not rewritten.

The card also listed four choices that agents had already made, and Jared left them as they were: the user confirms the technology choices at the end of the architecture step (line 1521); a checked image-generation route stays trusted for 7 days and is re-checked only when the user asks (K4, line 1345); conflict worktrees are durable records (line 1365); and the FileSafe trace defaults are 8 MiB per trace and 256 MiB per run (line 1330).
